question.text: Per the chapter, when is NAV typically computed on a DAILY basis (as distinct from the minimum monthly disclosure for open-ended Cat III funds)?

answer.text: When the Cat III AIF is investing only in listed securities
When the fund has less than INR 100 crore AUM

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter: 'In case a Category III AIF is investing in listed securities only, NAV is usually computed on a daily basis.' Daily computation supports MTM for exchange-traded positions. The Trap: AUM threshold isn't a valuation trigger. Year-end only contradicts monthly disclosure rule. Sponsor direction does not override regulation. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests valuation frequency. XXI-B tests similar for listed-PMS. Manager's Pro-Tip: Even if the PPM commits to monthly NAV disclosure, computing it DAILY gives the risk desk the telemetry to monitor leverage, drawdown and VaR limits live - otherwise limit breaches surface only at month-end.
